top_stories.title: World launches World ID suite for banks
points: World Bank/World launched a human verification system for banks combining identity verification, deepfake detection, and AI agent delegation.
The system acts as a middleware layer (intermediary software connecting different systems) between banking platforms and identity verification sources.

The bundle includes the World ID app, deepfake detection for Zoom (generally available after an April 2026 beta), and World ID for Agents (AgentKit), letting users delegate verification 'Proofs' to AI agents.
Over 18 million people hold a Proof of Human (a cryptographic credential verifying a user is a unique individual without revealing their identity).
Targets emerging markets where identity fraud and account takeovers pose significant risks to financial institutions.
Pricing and specific bank deployment partners remain undisclosed at launch.

unique_angles.point: Framed primarily as a World Bank initiative aimed at reducing fraudulent transactions and improving customer identity confirmation for banks generally.
Specified the product suite name (World ID suite), its components, and user adoption figures (18M+ Proof of Human holders).

items.title: JPMorgan Expands JPM Coin to Ethereum
points: JPM Coin (JPMD), representing actual JPMorgan bank deposits on public blockchains, expanded to Ethereum for institutional clients, following its Base launch in November 2025.
Enables peer-to-peer transfers across the EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine—a standard letting different blockchains run compatible code) ecosystem.
JPMorgan's Kinexys division has processed $4 trillion in cumulative transactions and averages $7 billion in daily volume.
Tokenized money-market funds were launched on Ethereum in December 2025 and May 2026.

items.title: Hyperliquid Retail Traders Lose $280M
points: Nearly 400,000 wallets have shown $280 million in all-time cumulative losses, with $126 million occurring since November 2025 across six consumer apps.
Fees account for slightly more than half of recent losses; stacked builder fees push per-$100 order costs to 6.5–14.5 cents, hitting small, frequently-trading accounts hardest.

Only 1 in 7 new traders remain active three months later, and about half of each month's active traders are first-timers, suggesting growth relies on constant new user acquisition rather than retention.

items.title: Stablecoin Payment Volume Surges 45%
points: Stablecoin payment volume hit $482 billion through September 2026, up 45% year-over-year, while total supply held flat at $305 billion—indicating higher transaction velocity rather than new issuance.
Card spending linked to stablecoins reached $3.9 billion, roughly 10x the prior year, with sub-$50 purchases driving 84% of transaction count growth.

Mastercard deployed its Global Money Platform, Stripe expanded stablecoin card coverage to 100+ countries via a Plasma partnership, and Visa's Inyo Global became the first commercial user of USDC prefunding.
Despite this growth, stablecoin card spending remains just 0.03% of Visa's $4 trillion quarterly volume.

items.title: Stripe Expands Link Agent Wallet
points: Stripe expanded its Link Agent Wallet to cover hotels, flights, subscriptions, and recurring billing across 100+ countries with multi-currency support.
This moves the product beyond single-purchase ecommerce transactions into broader recurring and travel-related payments.

The system functions as a middleware layer (intermediary software that connects different systems) between banking platforms and identity verification sources.
Implementation targets emerging markets where identity fraud and account takeovers pose significant operational and security risks to financial institutions.
